manufacturer_documents.device: Alberta Health Services CRRT alarm pathway for one machine family (PrisMax); applies to that family only

parameters.name: Access and return pressures
parameters.explanation: Access pressure reflects withdrawal into the extracorporeal circuit and return pressure reflects flow back to the patient. Interpret trends with the prescribed blood flow and assess the patient, catheter and tubing before acting.

parameters.name: Blood flow
parameters.explanation: This is the circuit blood-pump rate. Verify it against the prescription and review interruptions or pressure alarms; adjustment follows the authorized pathway.

parameters.name: Delivered dose against prescription
parameters.explanation: Compare the treatment delivered over time with the prescription. Downtime can lower delivered therapy even when the current settings match the prescription. Document interruptions and report shortfalls.

parameters.name: Alarm state
parameters.explanation: The displayed alert identifies the detected condition and assigned priority. Whether the pump stops depends on the alarm and model. Check the patient and follow the specific device instructions.

safety_concepts.text: Check the patient first, and review and address the alarm on the screen before clearing it; the alarm off, disable and override buttons decrease alarm sensitivity.
On the device described, the blood pump stops with high-priority (flashing red) alarms; other devices differ.
Confirm the chest radiograph required after internal jugular or subclavian catheter placement has been done and reviewed before first use (KDIGO).

Escalate possible heparin-induced thrombocytopenia promptly for clinical probability assessment. If clinically likely or confirmed, follow the authorized pathway to stop all heparin exposure, including flushes and locks.

monitoring_concepts.text: Monitor haemodynamics, temperature, fluid balance, electrolytes, acid-base results and bleeding.

escalation_concepts.text: If alarms cannot be resolved, assess the patient, notify the treating team and follow the device and local CRRT pathway for ending therapy. Return circuit blood only if the pathway and device instructions permit it for that failure. Document the cause and interruption.
Report bleeding, suspected HIT, access problems, haemodynamic instability and interruptions.

sources.use: KDIGO 2012: prescribing guideline; summary of Section 5 statements read
AHS Dialyzing Wisely CRRT alarm pathway (Jan 2025), device-specific (PrisMax), read in full

required_sources: The operator's manual for the model and software version used locally
gaps: Parameter notes explain general concepts and identify cited example models. Alarm behavior, button sequences and settings depend on the local model and policy.
Safety, monitoring and escalation statements are reused from the matching skill draft and retain their evidence status.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register. No proprietary screens, alarm tables or manuals are reproduced.
